domains.title: Tenancy, identity and the audit trail

models.name: Membership
models.comment: A user's membership of one organisation, carrying their role there.

models.name: LoginAttempt
models.comment: Rate-limiting evidence for authentication. FR-110.

models.name: AuthToken
models.comment: A one-time link sent to an address. Email verification and password reset are the same mechanism with different windows, so they are one table. Only the digest is stored: a link that leaks cannot be read back out of the database, which is the same rule every other capability in this product follows.

models.name: AuditLog
models.comment: Immutable record of every state-changing action. FR-109.

models.name: OnceRequest
models.comment: Transactional outbox. Domain events are written in the same transaction as the state change, then dispatched by the worker. At-least-once, so every handler must be idempotent. ADR-0007. One request, once. Phase 46. A key written before the work and checked before it is repeated. The browser mints it when the form is drawn, so every press of that particular button carries the same key and a second press lands on the unique index rather than on a second payment. A deliberate second payment comes from a freshly drawn form, and therefore a different key, and goes through. Rows are swept after a month: long enough to outlast any retry a provider or a person will send, short enough that this does not become a second copy of everything that ever happened.

models.name: SyncedAction
models.comment: One action a device recorded offline and the server has since applied. Exists for one reason: a flush interrupted halfway must not write everything again when the signal comes back. The device generates the id before it sends anything, and this table is the record of which ids have already been honoured. Only applied actions are kept. A conflict stays on the device with the reason it was refused, because the person holding the device is the one who has to decide what to do about it, and a row here would make the retry read as a duplicate and disappear.

models.name: ImportBatch
models.comment: A file somebody brought from another system, and what became of it. Phase 33. The rows are kept as they arrived so the mapping can be changed and the preview re-run; the report says, row by row, what did not go in and why.

models.name: Vehicle
models.comment: A physical vehicle. Exists independently of any owner or workshop. Globally unique by VIN. ADR-0004.

models.name: VinDecode
models.comment: What a decoder said about a VIN, kept so a VIN is asked about once. Phase 43. Not a workshop's data: a VIN's maker and model are the same whoever asks, so the answer is shared, and nothing in it names a workshop or an owner.

models.name: HandoverInvitation
models.comment: A sale waiting for the buyer to accept it. Phase 44. The seller starts it, from the portal or at a workshop counter; the buyer opens a link and accepts; only then does the ownership move. A partial unique index in the migration keeps one vehicle to one pending handover, so a car cannot be promised to two people. Only the digest of the link's token is stored, as with every capability in this product.

models.name: VehicleEvent
models.comment: One immutable fact about a vehicle. APPEND ONLY. There is no update path in the application. Corrections append a superseding event. FR-401, FR-406.

models.name: VehicleOwnership
models.comment: Who held the vehicle, and when. At most one open row per vehicle. V5.

models.name: OdometerReading
models.comment: Every odometer reading ever taken, including implausible ones. An impossible reading is evidence, not an error. FR-307, invariant V7.

models.name: VehicleAccessGrant
models.comment: A workshop's or person's right to read or write a vehicle's passport. A workshop earns write access by servicing the vehicle. FR-409.

models.name: PassportShare
models.comment: An anonymous, expiring, revocable link to one vehicle's passport. FR-409.

models.name: PassportShareAccess
models.comment: Every read of a shared passport, visible to the owner. FR-410.

models.name: VehicleDocument
models.comment: A key that lets something the workshop already runs read its records. Phase 18. The token is shown once and only its digest is stored, the same treatment as a session or a share link. A key belongs to one organisation and can read only that organisation's records plus the vehicle histories it is entitled to, exactly as a signed-in owner could. The vehicle's paperwork. Phase 20. Documents belong to the car, not to the workshop that scanned them, so a workshop with read access to the vehicle sees them and so does the owner. Nothing is deleted: a removed document keeps its row and its reason.

models.name: VehicleClaim
models.comment: A customer asking for a vehicle to be put on their account. A VIN is visible through a windscreen and a plate from further away, so neither is evidence of anything. Every claim is answered by a person at the workshop that serviced the vehicle, and the product never decides one on its own: it has no way to tell an owner from somebody who walked past the car.

models.name: PartFitment
models.comment: Which vehicles a part fits. Deliberately not inferred from anything. Guessing which pads fit a particular car puts the wrong pads on it, and the person who finds out is braking. Until a fitment provider is wired in these rows come from a person, and the absence of a row means nobody has said rather than that the part does not fit.

models.name: ProductSitePrice
models.comment: What one part sells for at one site, where it differs. Phase 44. Absent means the product's own price, which is the answer nearly always. A price here is a figure somebody chose for this site, never a percentage of a list that may move under it.

models.name: ServiceItem
models.comment: Catalogue of standard services with book times. FR-615.

models.name: ServiceSchedule
models.comment: Next service due, by date and by projected mileage. FR-1504.

models.name: FleetAgreement
models.comment: What a fleet customer has agreed. Phase 16. One row per company customer, and only for those who have negotiated terms. Its absence means list price, which is how every other customer is treated and how a fleet without an agreement should be too.

models.name: ConsentChange
models.comment: Every change to a marketing permission, kept forever. Consent is only worth anything if you can show when it was given and by what route. A boolean on a customer row proves nothing: it shows the current state and no history, and the one time it matters is the time somebody asks how you came to have it. Written by a database trigger, so a flag cannot be flipped without the trail.

models.name: Job
models.comment: The central aggregate. Everything in the workshop hangs off the Job.

models.name: JobStatusEvent
models.comment: The progress trail shown on the job screen. FR-604.

models.name: JobLabourLine
models.comment: Charged time. Distinct from TimeEntry, which is worked time. See the ubiquitous language in docs/02-design/01-domain-model.md section 2.

models.name: TimeEntry
models.comment: Worked time, used for labour cost. Distinct from JobLabourLine. A technician has at most one open entry. Invariant J5.

models.name: VehicleCheck
models.comment: The car as it was when it changed hands: arriving (IN) or leaving (OUT). One of each per job at most. Phase 35.

models.name: Signature
models.comment: Somebody's mark on a pad, kept as the strokes that made it. A record of its own, so the check-in, the check-out, an approval given across the counter, the terms and a warranty all point at the same kind of thing. Phase 35.

models.name: KeyEvent
models.comment: Where the keys went, each time they moved. Where they are now is the latest of these. Phase 35.

models.name: ServicePackage
models.comment: A piece of work priced and described as one thing: labour, parts, a checklist, a duration, a price and an interval. A job or a booking made from one starts with all of it on it. Phase 37.

models.name: ServicePackageCheck
models.comment: One thing to do and tick on a job made from the package.

models.name: JobSublet
models.comment: Work bought from another business and sold on a job. Phase 38.

models.name: EstimateShare
models.comment: The secure link sent to the customer. Unguessable, expiring, revocable.

models.name: EstimateApproval
models.comment: The recorded customer decision. Immutable evidence. FR-807.

models.name: LabourRate
models.comment: What an hour is charged at, at this workshop or at one of its sites. Phase 44. A list rather than a number, because a workshop charges differently for diagnostics and for an MOT, and a group charges differently in a city centre than on an industrial estate. A rate with no site is the workshop's; one with a site belongs to that site and wins there.

models.name: TaxComponent
models.comment: One tax inside a rate: a rate can carry a federal and a provincial tax, and a compound one is charged on the price with the taxes before it. Phase 41.

models.name: TaxEntry
models.comment: What each tax came to on a document, as it was issued: an invoice, a credit note (negative), a counter sale. Written once, never changed; the report per tax reads only these, so a rate retired later cannot change what was declared. Phase 41.

models.name: DocumentSequence
models.comment: Gapless per-organisation document numbering. A database sequence would leave gaps on rollback, which is not acceptable for tax documents. FR-902.

models.name: PaymentAttempt
models.comment: One try at paying some of an invoice through a provider. Phase 32. Pending, then succeeded, failed or cancelled, once; a succeeded attempt produces the Payment exactly once. The provider's own record is kept in providerPayload (the stub's memory; a real provider is asked instead).

models.name: CreditNote
models.comment: An issued invoice is immutable. Corrections are credit notes. FR-907.

models.name: Refund
models.comment: Money going back to a customer. Phase 16. A refund is its own record rather than a negative payment, because the two answer different questions. A payment says what came in; a refund says what went back, why, and against which credit note. Reporting that nets the two together silently loses the second answer, and the second answer is the one an argument at the counter turns on.

domains.title: The counter, gift cards and money held

models.name: Deposit
models.comment: Money held for a customer: a deposit taken before the work, or a credit kept on account after a refund. A liability until it goes against an invoice or back to the customer. Phase 30.

models.name: DepositMovement
models.comment: One movement of money held: negative when it goes against a bill or back to the customer. The taking itself is the deposit row.

models.name: GiftCard
models.comment: Money taken in advance for work not yet chosen. A liability until it is spent, never revenue on the day it is sold. Phase 26.

models.name: GiftCardEntry
models.comment: One movement on a card. Positive when loaded, negative when spent.

models.name: TillSession
models.comment: A day at the till. Opened with a float, closed with a count, and the variance between the two is reported rather than absorbed.

models.name: JournalEntry
models.comment: Every entry must balance. An unbalanced entry is rejected. FR-1202.

models.name: Expense
models.comment: Money out that is not a supplier bill. Until this existed these were hand-written journal entries, which works exactly as long as the person writing them knows double-entry.

models.name: Warranty
models.comment: What a workshop stands behind, and for how long. Cover runs from the day the work was done, not the day the part was sold, and it runs out two ways: a period and a distance, whichever comes first. A van reaches twenty thousand miles in five months, so a check that reads only the calendar gives away a year of free parts.

models.name: WarrantyClaim
models.comment: Somebody saying the work did not hold. A claim can be raised against expired cover, because a workshop does settle those out of goodwill and that decision is worth recording rather than hiding. What the database insists on is that a goodwill claim says why.

models.name: SupplierReturn
models.comment: Parts sent back to a supplier, from the delivery they came on to the credit note that settles them. Phase 38.

models.name: SupplierCreditApplication
models.comment: A credit note set against a bill the supplier is owed.

models.name: SupplierPayment
models.comment: Money going to a supplier. Phase 16. One payment can settle several bills, and one bill can be settled by several payments, so the link between them is its own table with an amount on it. A remittance advice is a list of those allocations, which is why they are stored rather than derived.

models.name: PayRate
models.comment: Effective-dated. A rate is never edited, only closed and superseded, so asking what an hour cost means asking what it cost on that day. ADR-0013.

models.name: AttendanceRecord
models.comment: On site and being paid. Distinct from TimeEntry, which is time on a job. The gap between the two is what utilisation measures.

models.name: Timesheet
models.comment: A pay period for one person. Approved once, then it stops moving: payroll is the one place where "somebody edited it afterwards" is unrecoverable.

models.name: Certification
models.comment: Qualifications with an expiry. An MOT tester whose licence lapsed is a legal problem, not a reminder, so this is queried rather than filed.

models.name: Skill
models.comment: A kind of work somebody can be signed off on. Named by the workshop, not by us: a truck garage and a tyre bay do not share a vocabulary.

models.name: EmployeeSkill
models.comment: One person signed off on one skill. The absence of a row means they cannot do it. That is deliberate: a NONE level would be a row asserting an absence, and the two would eventually disagree.

models.name: JobTypeSkill
models.comment: What a kind of work needs before somebody may be given it.

models.name: WorkingPattern
models.comment: When somebody is contracted to be here. Replaces the single `dailyCapacityHours` figure on a site, which was a number typed once and knew nothing about holidays, part-time hours or the apprentice at college on Fridays. One row per person per weekday they work; a weekday with no row is a day they are not in.

models.name: PayrollRun
models.comment: One pay period, exported once. Phase 16. The product does not run payroll. It hands approved timesheets to whatever does, as a file, and records that it did. The run exists so the same timesheets cannot be handed over twice and so the wages posting has a single document behind it.

models.name: PayAdjustment
models.comment: A bonus or a deduction on one person's timesheet. Phase 43. Added while the sheet waits for a run and fixed once the run has taken it, which the database enforces as well as the product. A deduction here is one the workshop agreed with the person; tax and pension are the payroll software's.

models.name: CommissionBand
models.comment: Marginal bands. The rate applies to the part of the basis above `from`, never to the whole of it: a cliff edge distorts behaviour at month end.

models.name: Conversation
models.comment: One thread per customer, and one per job when a message is about a job, whatever carried it. What went out and what came back are filed onto it. Phase 36.

models.name: MessageAttachment
models.comment: A file that travelled with a message, in either direction. Phase 36.

models.name: MessageTemplate
models.comment: A workshop's own sentences, filled from the job when sent. Phase 36.

models.name: StaffNotification
models.comment: Something that happened that a member of staff may need to act on, for them in particular. Each opens the record it is about. Phase 39.

models.name: SuppressedAddress
models.comment: An address nothing may be sent to. A mailbox that does not exist today will not exist tomorrow, and carrying on sending to it is how a sender's reputation is destroyed: providers read a high bounce rate as evidence the list was bought rather than earned, and start filing everything else as spam. Lifted by a person, never automatically. An address that starts working again is usually an address somebody corrected, and correcting it is the moment to say so.

models.name: DeliveryEvent
models.comment: One thing a provider said about a message after it left. Kept as its own rows rather than folded into the message, because a single message produces several and they arrive out of order. The message carries the conclusion; this carries the account of how it got there.

models.name: OperatorAlert
models.comment: Something a customer sent in. Matched to a customer and a job with a stated confidence rather than a silent assignment: a reply filed against the wrong job is worse than one filed against nothing, because somebody reads it about another car. What the operator has already been told about a signal. Phase 57. One row per signal rather than one per message: the question is whether this still needs saying, and a log of every alert ever sent answers that slowly. `sentAt` is when a message actually went, which is not the same as when the row was written — a signal recorded but never sent must still send.

models.name: ReviewRequest
models.comment: One customer asked how a job went. One per job, enforced by a unique index. Asking twice about the same repair is how a workshop teaches somebody to ignore it.

models.name: LoyaltyEntry
models.comment: One movement of points, positive or negative. The balance is the sum of these rather than a figure somebody edits, so it can never drift from the history that produced it.

models.name: Referral
models.comment: A code one customer gives another.

models.name: Coupon
models.comment: A code a customer hands over. Phase 45.5. Every promise a coupon makes is a column: when it starts, when it ends, what the bill has to reach, how many times it may be used at all and how many times by one person. A redemption is a row of its own, so "who used it and what did it give away" is read rather than inferred.

models.name: CouponRedemption
models.comment: One use of a code, against one bill.

models.name: AutomationRule
models.comment: A rule is trigger, conditions and actions. Deliberately not a graph: a rule cannot trigger a rule, because chained automation is impossible to reason about after the third link and impossible to debug at all.

models.name: AutomationRun
models.comment: One firing, against one subject. Written whether or not anything was sent, because "why did this not fire" is the question people actually ask.

models.name: AutomationAction
models.comment: A scheduled action, waiting for its delay to elapse. Kept as a row rather than a timer so a restart does not lose it and a person can see what is about to happen and stop it.

models.name: Campaign
models.comment: A segment and a message. The segment is stored as its rules rather than as a list of people, because a list goes stale and consent withdrawn on Tuesday must stop Wednesday's send.

models.name: AssistantExchange
models.comment: One exchange with the assistant. Phase 22. The prompt, the reply, whether a model touched it and what it cost, so an owner can see what the assistant is doing and what it is spending. The reply is what the person saw; a model's rejected output is not kept.
